merged.title: fix(port): draw Hoven ice beneath its scuff decals
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
Both ice layers on Hoven belong before the shrub pass. The translucent layer previously drew in the late effects pass and washed out the scuff decals. Mark the start of the RAC1 shrub pass so the earlier strips use the existing early effects pass.

## Verification

- Reproduced the washout and confirmed the restored scuffs in live RAC1 NTSC-U gameplay on Windows with Vulkan. Compared the captured draw list and the same in-game view.
- Built `openrac-rac1-ntsc` from the local disc on Windows after refreshing the managed source patches from `develop`.
- Passed `renderer_gif`, `effect_material`, host-hook parity, port conventions and layering.
- Verified the shared hook bindings for PAL, PAL v1.00 and NTSC-J from the release tables. Gameplay was tested on NTSC-U.

The capture uses the terrain and shrub draw boundaries. The game's debug draw mask can bypass this routing if it skips either draw.

merged.title: feat(sdk): require native mods to opt in to Vulkan access
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## What changed

- Native mods targeting API 1.20 declare `"vulkan_queue": true` to use OpenRAC's Vulkan handles, device setup, or native view images. Loading an opted-in mod keeps Vulkan rendering and queue submission on the game thread for the session. Mods targeting older APIs retain their existing behavior.
- The launcher and SDK packager validate the declaration. GitHub previews check the declared API version, and the installer checks the compiled library listed in the release ZIP.
- The starter template targets API 1.20. The SDK docs explain the opt-in and the planned Render Graph mod API.

## Verification

- Built `openrac-rac1-ntsc` and `mod_loader_test` on Windows, and ran `ctest -R '^mod_loader$'`.
- Passed the RAC1 host-binding parity check, port conventions and layering, and the SDK reference check and 68 SDK tests.
- Passed `cargo fmt --all --check`, focused launcher Vulkan tests, and launcher API version parity.
- Ran Vulkan smoke checks on RAC1 NTSC with opted-in, undecl

merged.title: fix(launcher): short Secret Agent Clank name, keep the subtitle whole
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody: **Before:** the launcher showed "Ratchet & Clank: Secret Agent Clank". On the desktop game page a long title could break inside the game's own name ("Going" / "Commando"). **After:** the launcher shows "Secret Agent Clank". On the desktop game page the game's own name moves to its own line, whole, when the title does not fit on one line. **How:** `withShownTitles` in `labels.ts` maps the shown name when the library is read. The game page splits the title with `titleLines` into two inline blocks; a two-part title never breaks inside a part. **Tested:** `yarn verify`, `yarn test:android`, browser preview at 960, 1024, 1200, 1600 and 2400 px and on Android. Not run in the Tauri app.

opened.title: fix(launcher): keep an installed mod the index has no archive of for this platform
opened.author: Promises
opened.untrustedBody:
## What

An installed native mod whose index entry has no archive for this platform (a hand-built copy, say) no longer holds back every other mod's update. Its installed version now fits as it is. Game, disc, API and revocation still count. A mod that is **not** installed still has nothing to install here (`NotForPlatform`, as before).

This is the follow-up I offered in the notes of #554.

## Why

- **Glawks' Weapon Wheel Pause publishes a Windows build only.** On Linux I built it from its release with its own CI steps. The game loads it fine, but it is in the index with only `windows-x86_64`.
- **`Resolver::pick` asked the index whether the installed version runs here.** `runs_here` failed it with `NotForPlatform`, so every set containing it failed to resolve.
- **The updater then held every update.** `mod_updates::plan` resolves the candidates together with what is installed. The failing mod is not a candidate, so there was nothing to blame and every candidate was held as "the set d

opened.title: feat(launcher): copy saves from the game's other disc
opened.author: farfeduc
opened.untrustedBody:
## The problem

Each disc has its own memory card (`memcard/<serial>/`). Build Ratchet & Clank from the PAL disc, play, then rebuild from the US disc: the PAL saves seem gone. They are still on the PAL card, which the US game never reads. This was asked for in the Discord's feature-requests ("Save compatible between version").

The saves themselves are compatible:
- every Ratchet & Clank disc (PAL v2.00 and v1.00, US, Japan) lists the same chunks with the same ids and sizes (`save_edit.rs`);
- Going Commando's US discs (v1.01 and v2.00 share `SCUS_972.68`, so one card) and its PAL disc have the same save tables (`save_edit_rac2.rs`);
- a save holds no language or 50/60 Hz setting: the options in it are camera, help, subtitles, sound and volumes (chunks 25 to 36).

Only the card's folder differs: `BESCES-50916RATCHET` on PAL, `BASCUS-97199RATCHET` on the US disc, `BISCPS-15037RATCHET` in Japan (the games' `func_00298BB8` template).

## What it does

The Saves panel shows **Copy from PAL

opened.title: feat(sdk): hero state entry, gravity mode and item update hook points
opened.author: Promises
opened.untrustedBody:
## What

Three new rac1 hook points for mods:

- **`rac1.player.enter_move_state`** (`Hero_EnterMoveState`, `i32(i32,i32)`, params `state`, `force`): `HeroEnterMoveState`, the hero's state change. One hook point over its 14 copies: L00 (levels 0, 4, 7, 9, 10, 13) and one each in levels 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 18.
- **`rac1.player.resolve_gravity_mode`** (`Hero_ResolveGravityMode`, `i32()`): `resolve_hero_gravity_mode`, the hero's gravity mode at the start of his update (0 the world's, 1 along the ground normal). One shared function on every disc.
- **`rac1.player.update_equipped_items`** (`Hero_UpdateEquippedItems`, `void()`): `update_hero_equipped_items`, the per-tick item update that also sets the item locks. One shared function; its three callers are calls, not copies.

## Why

A mod that gives Ratchet & Clank Going Commando's Gravity Boots in place of the Magneboots needs them. Everything that makes the Magneboots' magnet walk hangs on the hero's Magneboots fla

opened.title: feat(sdk): a hook point called as the game calls it, interface 1.21
opened.author: farfeduc
opened.untrustedBody:
A mod that does what the game does at a hook point sometimes wants the other mods' hooks there to apply. A mod's own weapon takes its rounds as the game's weapons do, and another mod's infinite ammo should cover it too. Until now the only way was `function()` with the game function's name in one disc's build (`FUN_L00_00233db8` on NTSC-U for `rac1.weapon.take_ammo`). That is another name on each disc, and nothing says that the function it returns goes through the hook chain.

Interface 1.21 adds one call at the end of the table:

- `hook_entry(name, signature)` finds the hook point as `hook` does (its id, name or an alias) and checks the signature the same way (`i32` and `u32` are one). It returns the function the game calls there: hooks.c's entry, by the point's symbol, which runs the mods' replacements (the mod loaded last first) and then the game's own function.
  - It can be called at any time.
  - It returns null for a hook point this OpenRAC lacks, another signature, or no functi

opened.title: feat(levels): match func_L30_0034C040 on both discs
opened.author: stephendolan2017
opened.untrustedBody:
## Function

Promote the existing plain-C draft of `func_L30_0034C040` into its shared Vidcomic source file. Levels 30, 32, 34 and 35 on both discs now build it from the same C definition with the file’s existing compiler flags.

## Why US level 30 used assembly

The draft matched the retail instructions in isolation. The conflict appeared when the US build placed its C object alongside the other functions in level 30. The US-native `func_L30_0034AAA0` already used two of the draft’s global names for different addresses.

| Name in the draft | Address used by `func_L30_0034AAA0` | Address this function reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `D_L30_001DD49C` | `0x001DD49C` | `0x001DD4DC` |
| `D_L30_001DD4A0` | `0x001DD4A0` | `0x001DD4E0` |

The placement check requires each symbol to have one address within a level. It rejected this object and kept the retail assembly. Adding the project’s caller suffix `_0034C040` to those two references lets each resolve to the address its caller actually read

opened.title: List auto-head-gear
opened.author: Promises
opened.untrustedBody:
Lists **Auto Head Gear**, https://github.com/Promises/rac1-auto-head-gear (v1.0.0, released by the SDK 1.20.0 workflow on every platform, with `SHA256SUMS`).

The Sonic Summoner and the O2 Mask work as soon as they are owned, as if worn, like in the later games. The game checks the head slot inside six moby updates: the sand mice and their houses for the Summoner, Blarg's toxic gas vents and Rilgar's extermibot and extermitank for the mask. The mod wraps those updates. When the item is owned, the head slot reads as that item for the length of the update, then it is put back. Ratchet's head is never changed visibly. It uses the behaviour catalogue's moby update hook points.

- `aiAssisted: true`: AI tools helped write it.
- **Tested** in game (NTSC-U, launcher 1.1.0): the sand mice answer the Summoner with nothing worn and with the O2 Mask worn. The gas part is not tested in game yet.
- `python3 tools/build_index.py --check-entry index/auto-head-gear.json` passes. The new version waits
